kill_fact: This run (28 July 2026) supersedes the 13 / 16 / 17 / 27 July shards, which independently reached the same REFUTED verdict; it re-confirms every load-bearing fact against primary sources and corrects ONE assertion the 27 July shard got wrong (see corrections (a)). The kill is structural, not scientific. (1) THE CATALYST DOES NOT EXIST AS A DATED EVENT. The board driver is FDA_approval_decision, but as of 28 July 2026 no BLA has been filed. The SEC docket for CIK 0001613780 since the 29 June 2026 8-K contains only the 16 July 10-Q, the 16 July results 8-K, and a Form S-3ASR -- no submission announcement, no acceptance, no priority-review grant, no target action date. The 16 July Q2/H1 release still carries only the forward-looking 'submission of the BLA anticipated in the third quarter of 2026'. A Q3 filing plus the roughly 60 days to a filing decision puts the first external gate around November-December 2026, and the approval decision itself in mid-to-late 2027: the value-resolving event is 12-15 months out and its DATE is not knowable for another 4-6 months. (2) THE SPONSOR'S DATE-KEEPING IS THE WEAK LINK. The Q3 2026 target is a documented slip from a 1H 2026 target the company itself announced in March 2025 as an ACCELERATION, moved on 29 June 2026 -- one day before the window expired. This is the third cycle on the same product after the December 2018 self-withdrawal over manufacturing and quality-control data and the August 2020 Complete Response Letter, and the 29 June 2026 FDA feedback lands once again on the CMC and biostatistical sections. That is the exact fault line that broke both prior cycles, not virgin ground. Priority review is also weaker than the bull carries it: DBV holds Breakthrough Therapy Designation and has said it INTENDS TO REQUEST priority review; the 29 June release makes no priority-review claim at all, and any grant is made at acceptance, not before. (3) THE FLOOR BREAKS. Verified cash is $174.9M at 30 June 2026, down from $229.0M at 31 March -- a $54.1M sequential burn -- against 296,061,497 ordinary shares outstanding per the 10-Q cover (five ordinary per ADS, ~59.2M ADS). Net cash is $2.95/ADS, backing 21% of the $13.90 price and decaying ~$0.90/ADS per quarter. There are no deal terms, no acquirer, no CVR, no asset-sale proceeds and no hard assets. The board entry's $9.50 floor is ~3.2x net cash with no cash, contractual or recovery basis; it merely marks a level above the 52-week low of $8.51, which was set BEFORE the December 2025 readout when the balance sheet was larger than it is now. (4) DILUTION IS ARITHMETIC, NOT RISK, AND CAPACITY WAS JUST RESTORED TO $150M. The runway guide of 'into the third quarter of 2027' expires INTO the same quarter the decision could land, at maximum information asymmetry, with H1 SG&A at $35.5M against $14.8M a year earlier as the company staffs a launch it has not been granted. The 17 July 2026 announcement refreshes the ATM to a total aggregate offering price of up to $150M under an automatically-effective Form S-3ASR -- roughly 11M ADS at today's price, ~18% of the ADS base, issuable at management's discretion. An undated single binary, 12-15 months out, with a $150M discretionary issuance facility in front of it and 21% cash coverage beneath it, is a story-stock hold, not a defined-risk special situation. (5) THE BULLS' ONE COMMERCIAL PROOF POINT INVERTS ON PRIMARY SOURCING. The bull thesis treats Stallergenes Greer's PALFORZIA discontinuation (effective 31 July 2026) as the competitive field clearing. The stated rationale kills that reading: the withdrawal is explicitly unrelated to safety, quality or efficacy and is attributed to complex administrative and dosing requirements that 'contributed to limited adoption in clinical practice.' PALFORZIA is the ONLY completed commercial experiment in this exact indication -- FDA-approved in 2020 for ages 4-17, the first and only peanut oral immunotherapy -- and it died of adoption, not of competition. A daily-wear patch requiring sustained pediatric compliance is not obviously the product that solves an adoption problem that killed a pill, and the read-across cuts directly at the $1.1bn peak-US-sales assumption carrying the entire $32 event-win leg. Approval and a business are separate achievements, and only the first is even in question inside the next fifteen months. The interrogator dossier reached the correct conclusion (SOFT_EXTENDED, verdict B, 'wait for the wash-out'); this check confirms its kill and refutes the board entry, not the science.
corrections: The material corrections run against the BOARD ENTRY and against the dossier's supply narrative; the dossier's numeric conclusion survives. (a) CORRECTED THIS RUN -- THE 27 JULY SHARD OVERSTATED ITS CASE ON THE SHELF. That shard asserted flatly that 'the 27 July shelf registration does not exist', reasoning from the absence of a 27 July press release on DBV's IR listing. That inference is invalid -- an S-3ASR requires no press release -- and it is contradicted by the docket: EDGAR carries exactly one DBVT Form S-3ASR in the period, accession 0001193125-26-316910, filed/accepted 27 July 2026 07:46:26 (CIK 0001613780). The 17 July 2026 press release, separately, states that a new automatically-effective S-3ASR was filed together with the sales-agreement prospectus supplement. The two dates cannot both be resolved from public secondary text and sec.gov direct reads were blocked (HTTP 403) this run; treat it as ONE refreshed-capacity event whose exact filing date is 17 or 27 July 2026 and do not build a narrative on either date alone. What is NOT in doubt and is what matters: ATM capacity now stands at up to $150M of ADS, automatically effective, drawable at management's discretion before the event resolves. (b) CONSEQUENTIAL LOGIC ERROR IN THE DOSSIER, UNCHANGED: positioning_washout and valley_of_death attribute part of the 16-24 July slide from $14.86 to $13.63 to a shelf filing dated 27 July -- after the window it is used to explain. Whichever filing date is correct, a 27 July event cannot have driven a decline that ended on 24 July, and if the 17 July date is correct then the dossier has double-counted a single supply event as two. Re-date it to one event and drop the second. (c) MATERIAL, SUPERSEDES AN EARLIER SHARD: an earlier shard corrected the bear text to '~$90M of ATM capacity remains' (the 5 September 2025 $150M gross program, ~$60M drawn in October 2025 at $13.00 and $14.00/ADS). That is STALE. The 17 July 2026 supplement refreshes the program to a total aggregate offering price of up to $150M, carrying forward registered-but-unsold ADSs together with newly registered capacity. The dossier's ~15% dilution haircut is defensible as a partial-utilization assumption on the refreshed total but must be restated as capacity-based, not as 'a further $150 million' of incremental supply stacked on the 2025 program. The dollar cap binds, not a share ceiling. (d) CATALYST: 'FDA_approval_decision' is not a scheduled event and must not be carried as a dated catalyst. The nearest external gate is FDA filing-acceptance roughly 60 days after a Q3 2026 submission (~Nov-Dec 2026) -- the first honest reconsideration point, because acceptance starts a real clock and reveals whether priority review was granted. catalyst_status SOFT_EXTENDED confirmed. (e) FLOOR: the board's $9.50 is refuted. Cash arithmetic re-verified on post-Q2 primary numbers: $174.9M / ~59.2M ADS = $2.95/ADS, decaying ~$0.90/ADS per quarter, 21% coverage at $13.90. The dossier's ~$6.50 blended figure is a reasonable mark-down estimate but must never be described as a floor -- nothing structural catches the price. (f) MINOR: the 29 June 2026 release contains NO statement on priority-review eligibility or Breakthrough Therapy Designation; bull_thesis leans on that release for a 'may be eligible for priority review' claim it does not carry. The supportable version is that DBV holds BTD and intends to request priority review. (g) MINOR, CUTS THE BEAR'S WAY: the 16 July release reports H1 2026 sales & marketing of $10.4M PLUS G&A of $25.1M -- $35.5M of SG&A against $14.8M in H1 2025. The dossier cites only the $25.1M G&A line against $14.1M, understating a ~2.4x overhead ramp and making the 'into Q3 2027' runway guidance harder to defend than the analysis already concedes. (h) RESOLVED FROM THE PRIOR SHARDS: the Q3 filing guide was REAFFIRMED on 16 July (not slipped again), the runway was extended to 'into Q3 2027', and no equity raise has been announced -- two modest positives. Neither repairs the absent date or the absent floor, since the extended runway still expires into the decision quarter. (i) SOURCING CAUTION, CARRIED FORWARD AND RE-TESTED THIS RUN: trade press (SnackSafely, 1 July 2026) reports a Q4 2026 filing target tied to a 6-month safety dataset from ~240 VITESSE / open-label-extension participants. NO primary source supports it; the 29 June 2026 8-K release and the 16 July 2026 Q2 release both say Q3 2026 and supersede it. Do NOT carry the Q4 claim -- but note the discrepancy is one-directional: if the Q4 read is right, every downstream date slips another quarter. (j) DATA-INTEGRITY FLAG, RE-CONFIRMED: FMP reports DBVT market cap $332.5M against a true ~$823M (59.2M ADS x $13.90) -- a stale share count understating by ~2.5x. Any screener ranking or valuation feed ingesting FMP market cap for DBVT is wrong; worth checking other recently-diluted ADR names. (k) PRICE ANCHOR: sop_breakdown and consensus_delta anchor to $13.63 (24 July close) while risk_reward and live_price use $13.90. $13.90 is correct -- it is the 27 July close (prior close $13.63, day range 13.635-14.13). (l) NOT DISPUTED: VITESSE met its primary endpoint (46.6% vs 14.8% responders, difference 31.8pp, 95% CI lower bound 24.5 against a prespecified 15 -- re-verified against the 16 December 2025 release this run), the FDA has requested no additional data, no safety objection has ever been raised across three cycles, and the balance sheet is not distressed today. The science is not the kill -- the absent date, the absent floor and the absent spread are. (m) THE $32 UPSIDE ANCHOR IS WEAKER THAN THE FILE CONCEDES: sop_bull's $1.1bn peak-US-sales input (at 3.5-4x peak) is never reconciled against PALFORZIA, the one market-tested datapoint that contradicts it, and omalizumab (XOLAIR), approved for food allergy broadly and now facing an interchangeable biosimilar, further caps single-allergen patch pricing power. This does not change the REFUTED verdict, which rests on the absent date and absent floor, but it means the 2.6:1 gross payoff is optimistic at the numerator, not only at the denominator.
